title: Homestead Foundry model registry
description: Schema v2 for a single model registry entry, across all three deployment targets. A registry file is a JSON array of entries matching this schema. The optional `target` discriminator selects which fields are required: omit it (or set it to azure-cloud) for a hosted Azure AI Foundry deployment, or name an on-premises target for a Foundry Local or Azure Local Foundry entry. See ADR-0018 for the rationale, models/README.md for the consumption contract, and docs/guide/model-selection.md for how an entry earns its status. IMPORTANT: this file and infra/types.bicep are a single unit of change. additionalProperties is false here and infra/main.bicep loads the registry through loadJsonContent against a closed user-defined type, so a field added to one and not the other breaks the Bicep build.

id.description: Stable, kebab-case identifier a consuming repo references. Never reused across two different models once published.

target.description: Which deployment targets this entry runs on, using the docs/targets/ slugs. ALWAYS AN ARRAY, even for a single target: Bicep user-defined type unions must be all literal values (BCP293), so a string-or-array shape cannot be mirrored in infra/types.bicep. OMIT for a hosted Azure AI Foundry entry: absent means ["azure-cloud"], which is why every v1 registry file remains valid unchanged. A multi-value array is for the shared ONNX core, the 35 aliases both on-premises targets carry (SPIKE-22); writing those twice guarantees the copies drift. azure-cloud may not be combined with an on-premises target, because no model runs both in the hosted service and on premises: the rosters are disjoint.

kind.description: Add new values here as new modalities are adopted; keep this enum authoritative and in sync with the union in infra/types.bicep. Do not let consumers infer kind from id or provider. text and speech-to-text were added in v2 because the on-premises rosters are text, reasoning, code, and speech-to-text only: neither on-premises target has an image, voice, or video model at all (SPIKE-22). embedding was added on 2026-08-02 when the worked-example account deployed text-embedding-3-large and -small to close the semantic-mapping gap; it is a distinct modality because an embedding deployment answers on the embeddings route, not chat completions, so a consumer that treats it as text will call the wrong endpoint.

provider.description: Prefer the vendor's own name (for example Microsoft, BlackForestLabs, OpenAI, xAI). For an on-premises ONNX build this is the publisher of the build, which reads Microsoft on every catalog row and is not the originating lab; name the originating lab in notes.

deploymentName.description: The name a caller passes as the model parameter. On azure-cloud this is the Foundry deployment name. On an on-premises target it is the catalog alias, for example phi-4-mini. For an entry whose status is planned or rejected, this is the name it would use (or did use) once deployed, not a placeholder.

sku.description: AZURE-CLOUD ONLY, and required there. For example GlobalStandard, S0. Forbidden on an on-premises entry: neither on-premises target has a SKU, and a value here would be silently meaningless rather than merely unused.

capacity.description: AZURE-CLOUD ONLY, optional. Provisioned SKU capacity for this one deployment. Omit to inherit the stack-wide modelDeploymentCapacity parameter. Per-entry because capacity units are NOT comparable across models and a single stack-wide value throttles the whole account to the smallest sensible number: on the worked-example account every deployment sat at capacity 1, which measured as 1 request per minute and made agentic tooling unusable. Raising capacity does not itself cost anything on a GlobalStandard deployment; billing is per token consumed, so this raises the rate ceiling rather than creating spend.

region.description: AZURE-CLOUD ONLY, and required there. The Azure region the deployment targets. Forbidden on an on-premises entry: inference runs on your own hardware, so there is no region. The Azure Local Foundry ARM resource does have a region, but that governs where its metadata and billing live and is a property of the cluster, not of a model entry.

variant.description: ON-PREMISES ONLY, and required there. The catalog entry name, for example Phi-4-mini-instruct-generic-cpu. SPIKE-22 established that the variant, not the model name, is the deployable unit on both on-premises targets: one alias fans out to several variants that differ by execution provider.

executionProvider.description: ON-PREMISES ONLY, and required there. vllm is Azure Local Foundry only and is GPU only. The QNN, VitisAI, OpenVINO, WebGpu, and NvTensorRTRTX providers are Foundry Local only: the Azure Local Foundry catalog sync paginates CPU and GPU only and never syncs them (SPIKE-22).

status.description: rejected entries are kept, with notes explaining why, so the decision is not re-researched later - never delete a rejected entry. No on-premises entry may be marked deployed until it has answered a real request (ADR-0019).

accessGating.description: For example none, limited-access: <url>, vendor-terms-acceptance. Use "none" literally when nothing gates access.

capabilities.description: For example text-to-image, image-edit, vision-input, word-timestamps, viseme-output, chat-completion, automatic-speech-recognition.

sizeNote.description: OPTIONAL, on-premises entries only. Free text, because the published catalog carries no size column and the honest value is usually UNKNOWN. Per ADR-0020 any number here carries its provenance as published, transferred, or observed. Never back-fill a size or a licence from an upstream model card: the ONNX build's properties are not the upstream model's properties.

notes.description: Short and factual. Longer rationale belongs in the doc sourceRef points at, not here.

sourceRef.description: Relative path to the spike, ADR, or backlog entry that backs this entry (for example docs/research/SPIKE-01-image-model.md).
